target_beneficiaries: Landholding farmer families with cultivable land
eligibility: Farmer family must own cultivable land as per the land records of the concerned State/UT
exclusions: Former or present holders of constitutional posts
Former or present Ministers and Members of Parliament or State Legislatures
Serving or retired government officers and employees, with specified exceptions
Retired pensioners receiving monthly pension of Rs. 10000 or more, with specified exceptions
Persons who paid income tax in the last assessment year
Practicing registered professionals such as Doctors, Engineers, Lawyers, Chartered Accountants and Architects
required_information: Aadhaar Number or alternative identity proof where applicable
recommendation_reason: The farmer may be eligible if they are part of a landholding farmer family with cultivable land and do not fall under the scheme's exclusion categories.
next_action: Verify that the farmer's cultivable land ownership is correctly recorded in the State/UT land records and complete the required beneficiary registration process.
source: PM-KISAN Operational Guidelines, Revised as on 29.03.2020

target_beneficiaries: Farmers growing notified crops in notified areas
benefit: Crop insurance coverage against specified crop losses
eligibility: Farmers including sharecroppers and tenant farmers growing notified crops in notified areas may be covered if they have an insurable interest and submit the required documents.
recommendation_reason: The farmer may be eligible for PMFBY if they grow a notified crop in a notified area and have the required insurable interest and documents.
next_action: Verify that the crop and area are notified under PMFBY and prepare the required land or tenancy documents and crop declaration.

target_beneficiaries: Farmers including owner cultivators, tenant farmers, oral lessees and sharecroppers
benefit: Timely credit support for cultivation and agricultural needs
eligibility: Farmers who are owner cultivators, tenant farmers, oral lessees or sharecroppers may be eligible for KCC.
recommendation_reason: The farmer may be eligible for KCC if they are engaged in agricultural cultivation and meet the applicable farmer eligibility requirements.
next_action: Prepare identity, address and land or cultivation documents and approach a participating bank for KCC application.
source: Kisan Credit Card scheme information, myScheme and RBI

benefit: Soil nutrient information and fertilizer recommendations based on soil testing
eligibility: Farmers can obtain soil health information and recommendations through soil testing under the Soil Health Card programme.
recommendation_reason: The farmer can use the Soil Health Card service to understand soil nutrient status and receive fertilizer recommendations based on soil testing.
next_action: Submit a soil sample through the appropriate soil testing facility and obtain the Soil Health Card.

benefit: Support for climate-resilient rainfed agriculture and water management infrastructure
eligibility: Farmers practicing rainfed agriculture may benefit from support available under the Krishi Bhagya programme, subject to applicable state guidelines and component-specific conditions.
recommendation_reason: The farmer may be a potential beneficiary if they practice rainfed agriculture and meet the applicable Karnataka programme conditions.
next_action: Verify the applicable Krishi Bhagya component and eligibility requirements through the Karnataka Agriculture Department before applying.
source: Government of Karnataka agricultural programme information
